---
title: Handle files
description: Upload a file's bytes, make the item that names them, download them, hand out a link that expires, and replace them.
---

A file is two parts: a blob, the bytes, and a file item that names the blob by its hash and carries the title and everything else. Upload the bytes, then create the item; anyone who can read the item can then read the bytes. [Files](/build/files) explains why the two are apart.

To upload, your key needs write on a type outside `system.*`, or the `blobs.manage` permission; with neither, Marfa answers `403 type_not_permitted`. To create the file item, it needs write on the item's type, such as `core.file`. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows. In the Swift examples, `copy` is an [open working copy](/reference/swift-sdk/working-copy#open-a-copy).

## Upload the bytes

[Upload a blob](/reference/api/blobs/uploadBlob) takes the bytes as the request body, **as they are rather than as a form**, with their media type as the `Content-Type`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs upload reading-list.txt
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /blobs
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: text/plain

<the bytes of reading-list.txt>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const { data: blob, error } = await marfa.POST("/blobs", {
  body: await readFile("reading-list.txt"),
  headers: { "Content-Type": "text/plain" },
});
if (error) throw new Error(error.error.message);
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let upload = try await copy.blobs.put(file: fileURL, mimeType: "text/plain")
guard let hash = upload.blob else { return }
```

Marfa answers the blob's `hash`, the media type it serves the bytes under, and their size:

```json title="Response" status="201"
{
  "hash": "sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0",
  "mime_type": "text/plain",
  "size_bytes": 34
}
```

The same bytes always give the same hash, so uploading them again **stores nothing more**. An upload adds no [event](/build/events): the item you create next does.

An upload has **no size cap and no total time limit**; Marfa ends one with `408 request_timeout` only when no bytes arrive for 60 seconds. While a store is still writing or deleting the same bytes, an upload answers `503 blob_store_unavailable`: try again shortly.

## Point an item at the bytes

Create a file item whose **`blob_ref`** is the hash. `core.file` takes any file. Use `core.file.image`, `core.file.audio`, `core.file.video` or `core.file.webpage` (an HTML page held as a file) where they fit, or a type of your own beneath `core.file`.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items create --type core.file --prop title=reading-list.txt \
  --prop blob_ref=sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0 \
  --prop mime_type=text/plain
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "core.file",
  "properties": {
    "title": "reading-list.txt",
    "blob_ref": "sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0",
    "mime_type": "text/plain"
  }
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: created } = await marfa.POST("/items", {
  body: {
    type: "core.file",
    properties: { title: "reading-list.txt", blob_ref: blob.hash, mime_type: blob.mime_type },
  },
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
_ = try await copy.items.create(Draft(
    type: "core.file",
    properties: ["title": "reading-list.txt", "blob_ref": .string(hash), "mime_type": "text/plain"]))
```

Marfa sets the item's `size_bytes` from the stored bytes. Soon after, a housekeeping job reads the bytes and adds what the item lacks, such as `extracted_text` or an image's `width` and `height`, which moves the item to its next version. `marfa items add reading-list.txt` uploads and creates in one command, and chooses the subtype from the media type unless you name one.

**Until an item names the hash, the bytes can't be read**, even with the key that uploaded them; only the owner and a key with `blobs.manage` can. A file item may name only bytes its writer uploaded or can already read, so upload with **the same key** that writes the item. Any other hash in `blob_ref` is refused `404 blob_not_found`, as a hash nothing holds is, so the refusal never reveals whether the instance has the bytes. [Files](/build/files#who-may-read-a-blob) covers a hash in any other property, such as an image link in a note's body.

## Attach a file to an item

To attach a file to any item, link them with an `attached-to` edge from the file item, as `marfa items attach <id> photo.jpg` does in one command. The file is then an **attachment**: it goes to the bin with the last item it's attached to, and comes back with any of them, as [Edges](/build/edges) explains.

On a device, a working copy links a body that shows the file, with `![](path)` or `![[file]]`, to it with a `references` edge, which **embeds** the file and attaches nothing.

## Find a file by its text

[Search](/build/list-filter-search#search) finds a file by any word of its `extracted_text`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa search quokka --type core.file
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /search?q=quokka&type=core.file
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

The housekeeping job runs every 30 seconds, so a file is found by its `title`, `description` and tags first, and by its text a little later. The job reads plain text and Markdown, web pages, PDFs, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files and their OpenDocument equivalents, and images while OCR is on. The instance's [configuration](/run/settings#change-settings-while-it-runs) turns it off (`enrichment_enabled`), turns OCR off (`enrichment_ocr_enabled`) and limits the text it keeps (`enrichment_max_text_chars`).

## Download the bytes

[Download a blob](/reference/api/blobs/downloadBlob) answers the bytes as they were uploaded:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs download sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0 --output reading-list.txt
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /blobs/sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const { data: bytes } = await marfa.GET("/blobs/{hash}", {
  params: { path: { hash: blob.hash } },
  parseAs: "arrayBuffer",
});
await writeFile("reading-list.txt", Buffer.from(bytes!));
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let bytes = try await copy.blobs.withFile(hash) { url in try Data(contentsOf: url) }
```

Marfa sends the bytes as an attachment named after the hash, never as a page a browser would show, so take the file's name from the item's **`title`**. A `Range` header such as `bytes=0-1023` gets part of a blob, with `206`.

A blob you may not read answers `404 blob_not_found`, like a missing one. `503 blob_store_unavailable` means no store could answer, so Marfa can't tell whether the bytes are gone: try again later.

A working copy fetches and keeps the bytes, as [Keep files on a device](/build/keep-files-on-a-device) shows. In the Swift SDK, read the file inside the `withFile` closure: the copy can remove it afterward.

## Hand out a time-limited link

An image element in a web page can't send your key. [Get a blob URL](/reference/api/blobs/getBlobUrl) answers a link that serves the bytes to anyone who has it, until it expires. `ttl_seconds` is its lifetime: **an hour by default, and at most seven days**; Marfa shortens a longer one, and the answer says what you got.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs url sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0 --ttl-seconds 900
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /blobs/sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0/url?ttl_seconds=900
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: link } = await marfa.GET("/blobs/{hash}/url", {
  params: { path: { hash: blob.hash }, query: { ttl_seconds: 900 } },
});
```

```json title="Response" status="200"
{
  "url": "http://localhost:8600/blobs/sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0/fetch?expires=1795048602794&signature=ea09307e75f2e6a367dfb3662577f47381d47c226e288ec89137113e984ad12a",
  "ttl_seconds": 900
}
```

Marfa checks your read **when it makes the link**, not when someone fetches it: revoking your key, or deleting every item that names the blob, doesn't end a link early. Ask for a link when you need one, with the shortest lifetime that serves, and **don't store it**.

## Replace a file's bytes

Upload the replacement, then update the file item's `blob_ref` to its hash, **naming the version you read**, as [Write safely](/build/write-safely) shows. **Clear what housekeeping read from the old bytes** in the same write, here `extracted_text`, and for an image `width` and `height` too: housekeeping only fills a field the item lacks, and Marfa sets `size_bytes` itself.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs upload reading-list.txt
marfa items update <id> --version 2 \
  --prop blob_ref=sha256:7623dfe0bbb9b127e9d68350ac7d9168fecfb3ac404778057b116315d3205780 \
  --clear-property extracted_text
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "version": 2,
  "properties": {
    "blob_ref": "sha256:7623dfe0bbb9b127e9d68350ac7d9168fecfb3ac404778057b116315d3205780"
  },
  "clear_properties": ["extracted_text"]
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: newBlob } = await marfa.POST("/blobs", {
  body: await readFile("reading-list.txt"),
  headers: { "Content-Type": "text/plain" },
});
await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id } },
  body: {
    version: 2,
    properties: { blob_ref: newBlob!.hash },
    clear_properties: ["extracted_text"],
  },
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let replacement = try await copy.blobs.put(file: newFileURL, mimeType: "text/plain")
guard let newHash = replacement.blob, let item = try await copy.items.get(id) else { return }
_ = try await copy.items.update(id, Edit(
    properties: ["blob_ref": .string(newHash)], clearProperties: ["extracted_text"],
    baseVersion: item.version))
```

The old blob stays **as long as an earlier version** of the item names it. Once nothing names it, housekeeping purges it at least `blob_cleanup_grace_seconds` (a day by default) after finding it unnamed, and never while a backup still names it.

The rules behind this guide are in the [blobs](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/blobs.md) chapter of the contract.
